subject: Post-demo: reserved throughput targets, streaming needs & GPU tradeoffs
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@finlytics.com>, Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & proposed next steps (throughput / latency targets)

Hi Elena / Aaron —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) SLO targets you shared: 95th latency <= 120ms for interactive queries (avg prompt length ~300 tokens), and sustained throughput target of 1,200 qps during market-open spikes. Correct?

2) Streaming: you need partial-token streaming to the UI for progressive results (websocket). We flagged this as high priority for UX.

3) Constraint: FinLytics prefers reserved capacity (Dedicated) for data isolation and predictable billing. Their initial ask is guidance on GPU type and reserved throughput for a pilot covering the equities product team (~10M queries/day peak).

Proposed next steps: 
- Aisha / Marcus: can we produce a short matrix comparing A100-80GB vs H100-80GB vs L4S (quantized) for the above SLOs, with estimated reserved throughput per GPU and expected 95p latency for a 300-token workload? (Action: sizing + rough cost delta) — due Tue 9/8 EOD.
- Elena: confirm whether 1,200 qps is sustained for an hour or expected as sub-15min spikes during market open. Also, share a representative request distribution if possible (percentile of short vs long prompts).
- I'll schedule a 30-min validation call next week to review the matrix and propose a pilot config + the trial window.

Attachments: sample request histogram (see attached spreadsheet) and our internal benchmark summary.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on streaming.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@finlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & proposed next steps (throughput / latency targets)

Thanks Dylan — correct on the SLOs: 95p latency target of 120ms is what product wants. The 1,200 qps number is what we see as a 20–30 minute spike around open (09:30–10:00 ET) with a tail for 45–60 minutes. Outside market-open, sustained qps is ~200–300.

Request distribution: roughly 60% <200 tokens, 30% 200–600, 10% >600. We'll upload a sample export to your Drive link by Monday.

Streaming: yes — websocket partials are required for the front-end.

On GPUs: open to your recommendation. Cost sensitivity is moderate; we'd prefer a model that meets SLOs with the smallest reserved footprint for pilot.

Elena
Head of Platform, FinLytics

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & proposed next steps (throughput / latency targets) — GPU comparison draft

Folks —

Draft notes attached. Short summary up front: 
- H100-80GB (fp16): best headroom for 95p <=120ms at 300-token median on a single model replica; estimated reserved throughput per GPU: ~450 qps (sustained), burst to ~600 qps with batching; cost delta ~+35% vs A100.
- A100-80GB (fp16): similar median latency but lower tail performance under concurrency; estimated reserved throughput per GPU: ~320 qps sustained; 95p edges closer to 140–160ms under concurrent streams. Cheaper baseline.
- L4S (4-bit quantized): lowest cost; per-GPU reserved throughput looks promising (~700 qps) for short prompts but 95p latency for >600-token requests degrades and streaming partials can increase CPU-side stitching latency. Good for read-heavy, short-prompt workloads.

Questions / tradeoffs called out in the doc: 
- If FinLytics is spike-driven (20–30 min open), adding burst pool (short-term reserved burst) could reduce baseline commit while meeting open-window SLOs — we show a hybrid reserve+burst config example.
- Streaming: our internal tests show websocket partials introduce ~10–20ms overhead per token sequence when stitching on our side; need to confirm front-end expectations for partial frequency.

Action items: 
- Marcus to add a simple pilot config (GPU count + reserved throughput + burst pool sketch) for a 30-day pilot.
- Dylan to propose pilot dates to Elena.

Attaching: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (tabbed: summary, per-gpu-estimates), gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf.

Cheers,
Aisha
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
Aisha Rahman | aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
From: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morris <elena@finlytics.com>, Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & proposed next steps (throughput / latency targets)

Dylan / Aisha —

Thanks for the draft. A few clarifications from procurement: for the pilot we'll need a simple committed monthly commit (1 month) with the ability to add a short-term burst addendum for market-open windows. Can you include an estimated cost for the hybrid reserve+burst config?

Also: regarding streaming, our front-end team expects partials every ~150ms of generated content; if your stitching adds 10–20ms that is fine, but we need to confirm end-to-end 95p under 120ms for interactive pages. If you can run a quick e2e check during the pilot that would help our sign-off.

We can target pilot start the week of Sep 20 pending contract redlines.

Aaron Cho
Head of Ops, FinLytics
